commits.message:
test(daemon): the fork-bomb ceiling test asserts how a refused daemon ends, not how fast it boots

The (ceiling+1)th daemon was given 5 s from spawn to exit. That measures
a Node boot on whatever runner it lands on, and it failed main's Release
run while fourteen process suites booted daemons at once. The breaker's
proof is that the daemon exits with failure and never binds its socket;
a daemon the breaker wrongly admitted never exits, which the test's own
timeout fails.

feat(click): every act a click or a lane switch causes is an effect the host performs once its turn has landed (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.lhy) (#772)

* feat(click): every act a click or a lane switch causes is an effect the host performs once its turn has landed (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.lhy)

A run, a slash line, open, copy, apply-update, relaunching Claude Code and
the band and pane surfaces are effects. The host performs a turn's acts only
once its config changes and trust-book answers have landed, in order, and
settles each with an effect-done. A slash line, a restart and a surface carry
the pane from the session's client hints. The tmux status row is held by
declaration in the renderer's subscriptions, not by an act.

Spec deviation from host-and-renderer.md section 7: PushedSurface acts are
band | pane only, the tmux row is a subscription, apply-update names no
version, and acts carry their pane. Section 7 is updated to match.

* fix(acts): the high review's fixes: slash lines one at a time per pane, the band outside tmux, acts a refused landing skips (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.lhy)

- type-slash runs in a per-pane queue, so two quick slash clicks no longer
  both read the bare input box and type into each other. A lane setup holds
  its session, and a slash for that session is refused while it does.
- The band act carries the session's pane or why it has none, so a session
  outside tmux still gets the mod installed and is told to type
  /reload-plugins itself.
- copy and open carry the session their click names, so their failure holds
  on that bar rather than on every bar.
- An act whose turn's changes did not land settles `skipped`: the changes'
  own outcome says why, so the reason is not held twice and a sessionless
  act raises nothing daemon-wide. The spec says so.
- The click fold classifies a thrown step with failureOf, so a close, a
  client that left, or a renderer that is down keeps its own class instead
  of becoming an operational failure.
- A run's facts move onto its act line, its only outcome line.
- A request whose session owes no lane setup allocates nothing.

* fix(acts): the medium review's fixes: a close answers closing, one queue per pane, acts in turn order (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.lhy)

- A turn the daemon's close stopped settles its acts `closing` again, so a
  click of acts alone is answered closing, not ok. Only acts whose changes
  were refused or failed are `skipped`.
- Whatever acts in one pane, slash lines, the band's /reload-plugins, a
  restart, a bar pane split, runs in that pane's one queue in the order
  asked, so a restart asked after a slash waits for it. Only a restart
  holds its session against slash lines; a split or the band's install
  holds nothing.
- Each act over in its turn starts once the one before it has ended, so two
  copies land in the order the turn asked.
- A declared session's row follows its newest request's pane, read where
  the declaration reads it, so a late older request cannot move it.
- A rate-limited copy or open says it did not run, on its act line.

* fix(acts): the second high review's fixes: setups in turn per session, a renderer start is one turn (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.lhy)

- A session's lane setups run one at a time, beside the one queue per
  pane: a band install ends, its /reload-plugins typed, before a restart
  the same click asked begins, and two installs never overlap.
- A renderer's start is one `start` turn carrying every live session's
  config, so its first output names every session it serves and the host
  releases no tmux status row or subscription it still holds for one.
- A rate-limited copy or open settles skipped, and its act line warns.
- The trust book's answer lands with the changes and is reported as they
  are, not as a performed act.
- A request that owes no lane setup builds nothing.
